name: Spotify
look: Near-black immersive canvas, one green accent, pill-and-circle geometry, uppercase tracked buttons.

hero.title: Sound, uninterrupted
hero.sub: Ninety million tracks, lossless from the first play, downloadable for the tunnel. No adverts between you and the record.

features.title: Built for listening, not for scrolling
features.sub: Everything that gets between you and the music, removed.

items.title: Lossless from the start
items.body: 24-bit playback on every track that has a master for it, with no separate tier and no upsell prompt.

items.title: Download anything
items.body: Take up to ten thousand tracks offline across five devices for the flight, the tunnel and the run.

items.title: Real controls
items.body: A ten-band equaliser, crossfade, gapless playback and normalisation you can switch off.

items.title: Group sessions
items.body: Hand the queue to the room. Everyone adds, everyone skips, nobody hands their phone around.

items.title: Credits that matter
items.body: Full personnel on every release — engineer, session players, studio and the room it was cut in.

items.title: Pays artists more
items.body: A user-centric royalty model routes your subscription to the artists you actually played.

showcases.title: A queue that knows when to stop
showcases.body: Recommendations weighted towards what you finished rather than what you clicked. Skip an artist twice and they stop appearing, without you having to find a settings page to say so.
points: Weekly mix you can regenerate on demand

showcases.title: Paid per listener, not per stream
showcases.body: Under a user-centric model each subscription is divided between the artists that subscriber played, so a thousand devoted listeners is worth more than a million passive ones.

metric_lead: Across the platform in the last quarter

gallery.title: New this week
gallery.sub: Editorial picks from the team, refreshed every Friday morning.

testimonial.quote: The credits page alone changed how I listen. I found three session players I now follow, and two of them have records of their own.
testimonial.name: Kwame Boateng

pricing.title: Pick your Premium
pricing.sub: Cancel any time, keep your library, and downgrade back to free without losing a playlist.

tiers.name: Family
tiers.desc: Up to six accounts at one address.

items.a: The account reverts to the free tier at the end of the billing period. Playlists, saved albums and listening history are all retained, and downloads simply become unavailable until you resubscribe.
No. Every Premium tier plays 24-bit audio wherever a lossless master exists. There is no separate hi-fi add-on.

items.q: How many devices can I use?
items.a: Sign in on as many devices as you like; play on one at a time. Offline downloads are limited to five devices and ten thousand tracks each.
Under a user-centric model, your subscription is split between the artists you actually listened to that month, rather than pooled and divided by total platform share.

cta.title: Start listening today
cta.sub: One month of Premium free. No card needed to try it, and no advert will ever interrupt a track.

footer.tagline: Ninety million tracks. No adverts between you and the record.

notes: The UI is achromatic by design — album art is the colour source. Green is functional (play, active, CTA) and never decorative.
Pill-and-circle geometry throughout: full-radius buttons, 50% circular play controls, 500px search pills. There are no sharp corners.
Button labels are uppercase with 1.4–2px tracking, which reads as a systematic label voice distinct from content text.
Type is a bold/regular binary — 700 or 400, with 600 used sparingly. Hierarchy comes from weight, not size.
The reference documents a compact 10–24px app UI scale; the display tier here extends it upward for a marketing surface, keeping the same weight logic.
